<reason>Side A (CON) built the cleaner path to victory. Its opening established three load-bearing arguments: population mismatch (seasonal permits don't serve protection-seeking families), pathways as additive rather than substitutive (Bracero networks, overstays), and enforcement producing genuine collapses (Australia, EU–Turkey, Israel). Pressure Q1 forced Side B to concede outright that Australia's boats stopped with no rerouting, and Side B also conceded [B4.3] that seasonal permits do nothing for Honduran mothers or Syrian families—concessions A exploited effectively by framing PRO's case as a "residual." Side B fought back well: the overstay paradox (A's own answer—exit tracking, employer verification, interior removal—is visa-system management, not border enforcement) and the "enforcement raises prices, substitution removes customers" framing were genuinely sharp, and B's graceful concessions with reframes showed skill. But B's fallback comparison ("the relevant population is labor migrants") never squarely answered A's weighing that a lever unable to move the largest share of flows cannot be the more effective lever, and B's scarcity response ("expansion is the motion") dodged the cap/lottery mechanics. Both sides used plausible background examples without fake citations; the Bracero timeline dispute ended in a wash. A's progression—concessions extracted, dispute narrowed, closing inversion point ("when PRO's framework needs enforcement to keep pathways from leaking, the motion has inverted itself")—gave the third-party reader the clearer reason to vote CON.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>The decisive sequence was A's Pressure Q1 on Australia (an island with no second corridor, arrivals near zero for a decade), which forced B into an explicit concession in [B4.1]—"Australia's boats did not reroute—they stopped, and I'll grant that plainly"—neutralizing B's central "every collapse is a rerouting story" thesis from [B2.1] and leaving A's strongest empirical example standing, only partially reparable via B's overstay pivot.</best_rebuttal>
